answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a grid where every agent must reach a mapped atlas to certify their position. An issuer acts as a geographic forge, assigning coordinates where each signed receipt proves an agent occupied the site. A verifier functions as a light-bearing lantern, replaying logs to detect latency shifts; any discrepancy beyond the noise floor triggers a permanent penalty. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs to reach sites, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion without relay help.
